top_choice_rationale: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock (Katori, Ye) is a new idea beyond the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes: an ensemble made insensitive to its own trap, reaching 1e-18 stability, reproduced and cross-checked by several laboratories, with systematic shifts that theory and experiment agree on, and it has enabled millimetre-scale redshift tests and constraints on constants. The two-name allocation is clean and the citation scope is tight. Twisted bilayer graphene (P001) is a major new field, but the unsettled pairing mechanism and the three-name attribution make it less mature for me; I still prefer awarding it to no award.
recusal_note: Professional proximity to atomic precision theory (calculations of clock-relevant atomic shifts) and long collaboration with the Lund and ETH attosecond groups, but no apparent direct collaboration with Katori or Ye from the profile; none requiring recusal apparent from profile.
